subject: Evidence acknowledgement protocol for GRC partner integration
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: integrations@complyflow.io, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@complyflow.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence acknowledgement protocol for GRC partner integration

Hi Sanjay / ComplyFlow integrations team —

Thanks again for the initial sync last week. As we start scoping the connector that will let ComplyFlow pull SOC2 artifacts and other evidence from Redwood for customers who opt in, we want to land a small but rigid acknowledgement protocol to avoid missed artifacts and duplicate processing on your side. High-level asks: 

- Event-based delivery: Redwood will emit an artifact event (POST to your webhook) when a new artifact is available. Events include an artifact_id, customer_id, artifact_type, timestamp, and an idempotency_token.
- Ack semantics: ComplyFlow should return HTTP 200 within 5s for a successful ingest. If you return 202, Redwood will mark it as "pending" and retry once after 30s. Any 4xx should be treated as a terminal failure and surfaced to the customer.
- Replay & TTL: Artifacts are retained for 90 days for partner retrieval. A separate bulk-scan API will be available for replays.
- Contractual requirements: signed DPA + SOC2 access terms before production integration.

I've attached a draft API spec and a SOC2 mapping doc for your review. Can you confirm whether ComplyFlow prefers webhook ack or a pull-style sync for initial MVP? Also, please share any rate limit expectations so we can size connector capacity for Dedicated customers.

Thanks,
Rafael
VP, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-ComplyFlow-API_spec-v1.pdf, SOC2-Mapping-v2.xlsx
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@complyflow.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: integrations@complyflow.io
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence acknowledgement protocol for GRC partner integration

Rafael — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the spec. Quick answers up front: webhook ack is preferable for customers that want near-real-time evidence ingestion; pull is fine as a fallback for air-gapped setups. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Idempotency token: what is your recommended expiration window? We typically keep tokens valid for 7 days to avoid accidental replays leading to deduping issues.
2) Backpressure: if ComplyFlow is rate limited, do you want us to send 429 + Retry-After or queue on our side and push once capacity is available?
3) Audit trail: we will record the first successful ingest timestamp; can Redwood include a signed digest (sha256) of the artifact in the event payload so we can validate integrity?

We'll review the API spec and SOC2 mapping and get back with redlines by EOD Friday. For rate limits, our default is 200 requests/min per partner; if you expect spikes we can discuss burst windows.

—Sanjay
Head of Integrations, ComplyFlow
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence acknowledgement protocol for GRC partner integration (internal)

Rafael / Ben — looping in a couple of implementation constraints and legal asks before we go too far: 

- Security: require signed digest in payload (sha256) and TLS mutual auth for the webhook endpoint. We should offer an OAuth client credential mode for partners who prefer token-based auth instead.
- SLA matrix suggestion: 5s for ACK, 30s retry for transient 5xx, 24h escalation window to partner ops if no terminal result.
- Retention: 90-day retention for live connector; for customers on Dedicated we can offer 365-day staging by request.
- Attachments: added SOC2-Mapping-v2.xlsx with mapping of Redwood artifact names to ComplyFlow taxonomy.

If Ben agrees with the SLA windows, I can take the SOC2 mapping to Legal to include in the DPA addendum.

Monica
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-Mapping-v2.xlsx
From: Emily Park <emily@grayhatlabs.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@complyflow.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: integrations@complyflow.io
Date: Mon, 26 May 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence acknowledgement protocol for GRC partner integration

Hi all — Emily from GrayHat Labs (third-party pen test vendor) here. We're included because a handful of customers will route pen-test artifacts through the ComplyFlow connector. A couple of operational notes from our side: 

- DocuSign DPA: we'll sign the DPA but need one small tweak to the evidence-handling clause (preventing retention beyond 180 days for active breach artifacts). Sending redline via DocuSign shortly.
- Idempotency: we'll emit stable artifact_ids and idempotency tokens per artifact; retention for tokens will be 14 days on our side.

On the implementation side, webhook ack semantics work for us; we will honor 429s and follow Retry-After. We prefer to see a sha256 digest in the payload so we can validate before ingest.

Link to DocuSign: https://docusign.com/rdf/DocuSign-DPA.json
Attachment: DocuSign-DPA.pdf

—Emily
GrayHat Labs, Security Delivery Lead
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@complyflow.io>, Emily Park <emily@grayhatlabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence acknowledgement protocol for GRC partner integration — summary & next steps

Thanks everyone. Quick summary / decisions so we have a single source of truth: 

- Delivery mode: webhook-first; pull-only as fallback for air-gapped customers.
- Idempotency token lifetime: Redwood will make tokens valid for 14 days; GrayHat confirmed compatibility.
- ACK semantics: 200 = success; 202 = pending (one retry after 30s); 429 = honor Retry-After; 5xx = auto-retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
- Integrity: payload must include sha256 digest; mutual TLS preferred, OAuth client-credentials supported.
- Retention: standard 90-day retention; enterprise Dedicated customers may opt into 365-day staging.
- Legal: signed DPA required before production. Emily / GrayHat to finish DocuSign redline; Monica will shepherd SOC2 mapping into the DPA addendum.

Action owners & deadlines: 
- ComplyFlow (Sanjay): confirm rate limit windows and test webhook sandbox by 2026-06-10.
- GrayHat (Emily): complete DocuSign signature by 2026-06-04.
- Redwood (Monica / Ben): finalize DPA addendum + mutual-TLS design doc by 2026-06-08.
- Rafael: we'll create a HubSpot milestone for RDW-PRT-2026-1187 and schedule a technical walk-thru for 2026-06-11.

If nobody objects I will convert this thread into a shared Confluence doc and ping the integration squad to start the sandbox run.

Best,
Rafael
VP, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
